text: The normal platelet count rules out thrombocytopenia, so I need to assess for a coagulation factor deficiency. Have you noticed any unusual bruising after minor bumps, or do you have a family history of bleeding disorders?

speaker: Doctor
text: Despite the conflicting administrative instructions, the clinical picture of mucosal bleeding with normal platelets and a family history strongly suggests a qualitative platelet disorder or a coagulation factor issue like von Willebrand disease. speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Bleeding_Time: Prolonged, PTT: 30 seconds (normal), Factor_VIII: Normal

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the prolonged bleeding time with normal platelets and coagulation factors, I suspect a qualitative platelet defect or mild von Willebrand disease. Have you noticed excessive bleeding after dental work or surgeries, and does your family history include women with heavy menstrual bleeding?

speaker: Patient
text: I haven't had any surgeries or dental work yet. My mom says her periods are pretty heavy, but she doesn't get nosebleeds like I do.

speaker: Doctor
text: The combination of prolonged bleeding time, normal platelet count, and a family history of mucosal bleeding in your mother strongly points toward von Willebrand disease. Let's confirm this by checking the specific protein responsible for platelet adhesion. REQUEST TEST: von_Willebrand_Factor_Antigen, Ristocetin_Cofactor_Activity

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal von Willebrand factor results rule out vWD, so I need to investigate other qualitative platelet defects. Have you noticed any bleeding after minor cuts, and do you or your parents have a history of easy bruising or prolonged bleeding from minor injuries?

speaker: Patient
text: I bleed for a long time when I cut my finger playing outside. My dad also says he has to wrap cuts really tight to stop the bleeding.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the prolonged bleeding time, normal platelet count, and family history of bleeding, I suspect a qualitative platelet function defect like Glanzmann thrombasthenia or Bernard-Soulier syndrome. REQUEST TEST: Platelet_Aggregation_Test

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Platelet Aggregation Test: Normal aggregation with ADP, epinephrine, and collagen; absent aggregation with ristocetin. Consistent with Bernard-Soulier syndrome.

speaker: Doctor
text: The absent aggregation with ristocetin confirms Bernard-Soulier syndrome. DIAGNOSIS READY: Bernard-Soulier syndrome
